clarifications.why: The contract requires an ISO-4217 currency code and defaults to THB, but the only currency evidence in the file is an ambiguous '$' symbol. Labelling it wrongly would misprice every product downstream, and the operator forbade inferring currency or converting FX.
clarifications.question: Every Net price cell is written with a '$' prefix (e.g. '$1234.56', '$1279') and there is no currency column. Does that '$' mean the prices are in USD (label them USD, no FX conversion), or is it a display artefact and the prices are really THB?

open_questions: Every Net price cell is written with a '$' prefix (e.g. '$1234.56', '$1279') and there is no currency column. Does that '$' mean the prices are in USD (label them USD, no FX conversion), or is it a display artefact and the prices are really THB?

notes: Currency is unresolved: the Net price values are rendered with a '$' prefix ('$1234.56', '$1279') and there is no currency column in the file, while the target schema defaults /currency to THB with a ^[A-Z]{3}$ pattern. Per the operator instruction not to infer currency or convert FX, no /currency mapping is asserted here; the operator must state whether the '$' is a display artefact (prices truly THB) or the prices are USD to be labelled as such without conversion.

Source tax facts are explicit and used as-is: every row says Tax included = 'No' (vat_included false) and Tax rate = '5%' (0.05). These are fixture values and are recorded from the file, not applied as real tax advice; no VAT add/remove arithmetic is performed.

The profiler typed SKU as int (min 470001, max 470012 yet top_values '00470001'), so the leading zeros are present in the raw text and would be lost by a numeric read. SKU must be cast to string without strip_leading_zeros, per the operator requirement to preserve leading zeros.

SKU also carries a barcode_like hint (8 numeric digits). It is used as /sku (unique identity key); /barcode is left unmapped because no separate barcode/EAN column exists and duplicating the item code into /barcode would fabricate an attribute.

No columns exist for brand, category, description, inventory (warehouse/qty/reserved), or promotions (code/type/dates/discounts), and no second sheet or hidden columns are present, so those contract pointers remain unpopulated rather than filled with invented constants.
Dates are absent from this export, so /prices/*/effective_from and /prices/*/effective_to stay null; the /prices collection therefore has one element per SKU identified by price_list 'standard'.

tables.reason: Single flat export with one row per item: a unique item code (SKU 00470001…00470012, 12 distinct of 12) plus a product name plus exactly one price-list entry ('standard') and its price/tax attributes. No warehouse, promotion, or category columns exist, so this is the product master sheet with an embedded single price record per SKU.

columns.name: SKU
columns.reason: Header 'SKU' is the primary product-code synonym; 12 distinct values for 12 rows (unique_ratio 1.0), no nulls. Values are 8-digit codes with leading zeros (top_values '00470001'…), so the column must be read as text and cast with strip_leading_zeros NOT applied — the zeros are part of the customer code.

columns.name: Product name
columns.reason: Header 'Product name' matches the product_name synonym list exactly; 12 distinct non-null values, one per SKU (e.g. 'SIM neutral 1'). Generic neutral test descriptions — no business meaning to extract, but they are the display names.

columns.name: Sales unit
columns.reason: Header 'Sales unit' matches the unit.sell synonyms ('sales unit', 'uom'); single constant value 'PCS' across all 12 rows, which is in the sell_unit enum_hint and resolvable by unit_normalize without a synonyms override. No pack-size column exists, so /unit/pack_size stays null.

columns.name: Price list
columns.reason: Header 'Price list' matches the price.list_name synonyms; constant value 'standard' on every row, which is also the schema default for price_list — carried explicitly rather than relying on the default.

columns.name: Net price
columns.reason: Header 'Net price' maps to price.amount ('net price', 'price' synonyms); float, never empty, 12 distinct values 1234.56–1356.77, i.e. one price point per SKU. Values are displayed with a currency prefix ('$1234.56', '$1279'), which must be parsed with parse_number_th. The prefix is the only currency evidence in the file and conflicts with the schema's THB default — flagged in notes rather than resolved.

columns.name: Tax included
columns.reason: Header 'Tax included' matches the vat_included synonyms; constant 'No' on all 12 rows, which parse_bool reads as false. This is an explicit source statement that the net prices are VAT-exclusive, so vat_included=false is used directly and vat_adjust is not applied.

columns.name: Tax rate
columns.reason: Header 'Tax rate' matches price.vat_rate; constant '5%' (percent-hinted, distinct=1). Parsed with parse_number_th percent_to_fraction → 0.05. The source states an explicit rate, so it overrides the schema default of 0.07; the fixture value is not treated as a real-world tax conclusion.

clarifications.why: The contract requires an ISO-4217 currency code and defaults to THB, but the only currency evidence in the file is an ambiguous '$' symbol. Labelling it wrongly would misprice every product downstream, and the operator forbade inferring currency or converting FX.
clarifications.question: Every Net price cell is written with a '$' prefix (e.g. '$1234.56', '$1279') and there is no currency column. Does that '$' mean the prices are in USD (label them USD, no FX conversion), or is it a display artefact and the prices are really THB?

changes_from_draft: /sku now uses cast(trim(SKU), to string) so the zero-padded codes '00470001'..'00470012' are preserved as text (confidence 0.96).
/prices/*/price_list now reads the source 'Price list' column ('standard' on all 12 rows) instead of a hard-coded constant.
/prices/*/vat_included now derives from the explicit 'Tax included' = 'No' flag via parse_bool with a false default, rather than a bare constant (still false for every row).
Added /prices/*/vat_rate = parse_number_th('Tax rate', percent_to_fraction=true) → 0.05, an explicit source value that overrides the schema default 0.07; 'Tax rate' is no longer an unmatched column.

Added a /currency mapping driven by the '$' prefix in the price cells, held at confidence 0.4 and paired with exactly one clarification (target /currency, action value_map, source_value '$'); no FX conversion is performed.
/prices dedupe_keys set to ['/price_list'] matching the contract identity keys for the collection; normalize_keys trim+upper retained.

Unit pack size, brand, category, description, barcode, inventory and promotions have no source columns in this single flat export, so those pointers stay unmapped rather than being filled with invented constants; remaining columns flow through /attributes passthrough.
